EV maker with massive burn rate, no profit, and existential dependence on cheap capital. ROIC deeply negative. Tight Fed = funding crisis. Negative ROIC is the screener's clearest avoid signal.

Your own screener shows ROIC = -79.62%. This is the clearest avoid signal in the scan. Hydrogen fuel cells with massive burn, no profit, subsidy-dependent business model. The screener identified this before the thesis broke down.

No moat, losing market share to competitors, high debt. Revenue growth stalling. No inflation protection and no pricing power against rising healthcare cost pressures. Classic ZIRP-era story stock now exposed.

avCons.why: Online furniture is first discretionary cut when gas eats household budgets. High debt, no moat, razor-thin margins. Double compression: earnings fall AND investors reprice the multiple simultaneously. Stagflation = existential threat.

Used car market is rate-sensitive. High inventory financing costs plus consumer credit stress equals margin collapse. Already came close to bankruptcy once. High rate environment is existentially threatening again.

Discretionary fitness spend evaporates when real wages fall and energy bills rise. Brand recovery story has failed repeatedly. Avoid legacy turnarounds in stagflation — the macro compounds the operational difficulty.
Restaurant spending is cut when oil eats household budgets. Labor cost inflation plus food cost inflation simultaneously compresses margins. Multiple compression follows earnings compression.

avReit.why: Entire REIT sector acts as leveraged long bond. Every 25bps increase in 10Y yield compresses REIT valuations 3-5%. Hold only after first confirmed Fed cut. Watch Groman signal #3.
NYC office REIT facing WFH occupancy crisis PLUS rate pressure. Double structural headwind. Office real estate is in secular decline regardless of macro environment. Avoid entirely.

Premium office REIT with high leverage and remote work secular headwind. Rate-sensitive debt structure makes this a spread product in a bad spread environment. Structural and cyclical headwinds simultaneously.
Healthcare REIT with tenant stress (Steward Health Chapter 11 bankruptcy). Dividend at risk. Avoid until balance sheet clarity restored and rate environment improves significantly.

avStory.why: EV charging infrastructure with no profit and heavy subsidy dependence. Tesla Supercharger network becoming industry standard creates structural competitive disadvantage. No moat, no ROIC, no path to profitability without QE.

Revenue declining, negative ROIC, no pricing power, fading brand. Plant-based food premium disappears first when consumers feel squeezed. No moat in any scenario. Classic ZIRP-era story stock fully exposed.

Accounting concerns and governance issues create existential risk beyond the macro. Even in QE scenario, company-specific risk dominates. Avoid story stocks with governance red flags regardless of AI narrative.

avInd.why: Spun-off aerospace at stretched valuation post-GEV separation. Defense budget uncertainty plus rate exposure to pension obligations. Prefer GEV over GE for energy infrastructure theme.
EV truck startup with negative ROIC, no production scale, and funding crisis. Existential in any tight-money environment. Your screener's signals (ROIC, Piotroski) all fail simultaneously.
Hydrogen truck startup with history of fraud allegations, no revenue, massive burn rate. Avoid entirely — company-specific risk plus macro headwind creates double danger.

hioil.r: ROIC 11.2%, Piotr:5, GC:1, 3.4% div -- high oil = peak earnings; USD revenues dominate
hioil.desc: ExxonMobil generates ~70% of revenue in USD. High oil directly expands margins -- every $10/barrel increase adds ~$4B to annual earnings. Strong dollar means international competitors are less competitive. 3.4% dividend is secure at $60+ oil.

hioil.r: ROIC 9.8%, 4.1% div -- Permian Basin low break-even; high oil + strong dollar = cash machine
hioil.desc: Chevron is the lowest break-even major oil company. Permian Basin operations generate strong free cash flow at $60+ oil. At $90+, Chevron becomes a cash machine. 4.1% dividend growing. Strong balance sheet -- can buy back stock aggressively at high oil prices.

hioil.r: Buffett-backed; high oil = massive FCF; OxyChem chemical division benefits from USD strength
hioil.desc: Buffett owns 28%+ of OXY -- when oil is high, the cash flow is extraordinary. OxyChem (chemicals) benefits from USD strength as competing global producers face FX headwinds. Most leveraged to oil price of the majors.

hioil.r: ROIC 15.31%, GC:1 -- consumers shift TO Walmart when energy costs squeeze budgets
hioil.desc: When gas prices are high and real incomes fall, consumers trade down to Walmart. Domestic US revenue base protects from dollar strength. Grocery dominance = inelastic demand. The classic high-oil defensive play.

hioil.r: ROIC 33.56%, Piotr:5, GC:1 -- bulk buying saves members money; membership fee is inflation-proof
hioil.desc: Costco bulk model is designed for high-cost environments. Members join to beat inflation. Annual membership fee is recession-proof recurring revenue. Domestic US bias protects from dollar headwinds. 33.56% ROIC is exceptional for retail.

hioil.r: ROIC 10.98%, Piotr:5, GC:1 -- refiner margins widen when crude stays high; USD revenues
hioil.desc: Refiners like Marathon benefit from supply-constrained high oil because crack spreads (refining margins) widen. They buy crude and sell refined products, both priced in USD. Strong dollar makes imported refined products more expensive, protecting domestic margins.

hioil.r: ROIC 20.91%, 2.8% div -- Tide/Gillette/Pampers have 60yr proven pricing power through oil shocks
hioil.desc: P&G has raised prices through every inflationary cycle since 1962 without losing market share. USD revenue base benefits from dollar strength. Essential products like Tide, diapers, and toothpaste have near-zero demand elasticity regardless of oil prices.

hioil.r: GC:1, 2.9% div -- high oil = Middle East tension = defense budgets surge; USD contracts only
hioil.desc: Lockheed is a direct geopolitical tension beneficiary. High oil from Middle East instability always triggers defense budget increases across NATO and Gulf states. 100% USD-denominated contracts -- dollar strength is a direct tailwind. F-35 and missile defense backlog extends 5+ years.

hioil.r: GC:1 -- Patriot/Tomahawk/Pratt+Whitney; Iran tension = defense demand spike; all USD contracts
hioil.desc: RTX makes Patriot missile systems, Tomahawk cruise missiles, and Pratt & Whitney jet engines. Iran tensions directly drive demand for Raytheon air defense systems. All US government contracts in USD. High oil = more Middle East tension = more defense orders.

hioil.r: ROIC 19.03%, Piotr:5, 2.6% div -- 130yr brand; passes oil-driven input costs through every time
hioil.desc: Coca-Cola has survived and profited through every oil shock in history. When transportation and packaging costs rise (both oil-driven), KO raises prices and consumers keep buying. The dividend has grown for 62 consecutive years through every inflationary cycle. Recession-proof cash flow machine.

hioil.r: ROIC 8.73%, PE:7.6, 3.9% div -- spice/flavor monopoly; zero substitution under cost pressure
hioil.desc: McCormick supplies spices and flavorings to every major food manufacturer globally. They cannot be substituted. PE of 7.6 is extremely cheap for a monopoly. In high-oil scenarios, food companies pass costs through and McCormick rides along with 3.9% yield.

hioil.r: ROIC 11.92%, Piotr:3, GC:1 -- break-even below $40; high oil = extraordinary FCF; USD revenues
hioil.desc: EOG is the best-run US shale company. Break-even below $40/barrel means at $90+ oil, EOG generates extraordinary free cash flow. Pays a growing dividend and buys back stock aggressively. Pure USD revenue stream -- dollar strength is neutral to positive.

carrytrade.r: Direct long-yen ETF -- the cleanest pure-play hedge against a carry trade unwind
carrytrade.desc: FXY holds physical yen deposits and tracks USD/JPY inversely. When the carry trade unwinds and USD/JPY crashes (yen strengthens), FXY rises directly. The simplest, most liquid way to hedge a portfolio against carry-unwind risk without shorting individual stocks.

carrytrade.r: Classic multi-cycle carry-unwind victim -- EM currencies and equities were funded by the same cheap-yen liquidity
carrytrade.desc: Emerging markets are financed disproportionately by carry-trade liquidity -- cheap yen (and dollar) borrowing flows into higher-yielding EM assets. Every major carry unwind (1998, 2008, 2015, Aug 2024) hit EM equities and currencies hardest as that liquidity reverses violently.

carrytrade.r: Flight-to-quality winner -- carry unwind panics send capital into long Treasuries as yields plunge
carrytrade.desc: When carry trades unwind violently, capital rushes into the safest, most liquid asset on earth: long-duration US Treasuries. Yields fall sharply as investors accept lower returns for safety, driving TLT higher. This was a clear pattern during the August 2024 unwind and the 2008/2015 carry unwinds before it.

carrytrade.r: Medium-duration flight-to-quality play -- less volatile than TLT but same safe-haven mechanics
carrytrade.desc: IEF offers the same flight-to-quality benefit as TLT during a carry unwind but with less duration risk (7-10yr vs 20yr+). A more conservative way to position for carry-unwind tail risk while still capturing the yield-decline benefit.

carrytrade.r: Short Treasuries — park cash when carry unwind hits without 20-year duration risk
carrytrade.desc: SHY is T-bills-adjacent. Use it as the conservative carry-unwind cash sleeve when TLT duration is too much.

carrytrade.r: Gold miners — unwind winner as leveraged funds bid the metal after the liquidation
carrytrade.desc: During a yen-carry crash, gold often catches the bid after the first wave of liquidation. GDX is the high-beta way to own that bounce.

strongdollar.r: GC:1, 2.9% div -- Bretton Woods 2.0 core pick; 100% USD contracts + world chaos = peak defense spending
strongdollar.desc: Lockheed Martin is the ultimate Bretton Woods 2.0 beneficiary. World chaos forces nations to buy US defense (F-35, Patriot, THAAD) all priced in USD. Strong dollar = cheaper for foreign buyers in local currency. Every geopolitical dollar spent flows through LMT. 5-year backlog expanding.

strongdollar.r: GC:1 -- Patriot missiles + Pratt engines; Iran tension + strong dollar = demand surge; all USD contracts
strongdollar.desc: RTX Corporation (Raytheon + Pratt & Whitney) benefits from Iran-driven tension AND dollar strength. Foreign nations need USD to buy Patriot systems -- increasing dollar demand while boosting RTX. The Bretton Woods 2.0 thesis and RTX revenues are literally the same trade.

strongdollar.r: GC:1 -- B-21 Raider stealth bomber + space systems; pure US government USD revenue stream
strongdollar.desc: Northrop Grumman makes the B-21 stealth bomber, space systems, and nuclear command infrastructure. 100% US government USD revenue -- zero overseas translation risk. Strong dollar = more foreign defense spending flows to US firms = Northrop wins alongside LMT and RTX.

strongdollar.r: Direct DXY long ETF -- the cleanest pure-play on the Bretton Woods 2.0 thesis in one ticker
strongdollar.desc: UUP tracks long USD vs basket of currencies. The simplest, most direct way to invest in the strong dollar thesis from the video. When DXY goes from 101 to 110, UUP gains proportionally. Inverse to GLD, IBIT, and DBC. When you believe the thesis, this is the clearest expression.

strongdollar.r: Small caps = 80%+ domestic US revenue -- direct strong dollar beneficiary vs S&P multinationals
strongdollar.desc: The Russell 2000 small cap index is the single strongest historical beneficiary of DXY strength. Small companies average 80%+ domestic US revenue vs S&P 500 at ~60% domestic. No EPS headwind from currency translation. When DXY rises 10%, S&P loses 2-4% EPS, IWM loses near zero.

strongdollar.r: Regional banks: 100% domestic revenue + high US rates = NIM expansion + foreign capital inflows seeking yield
strongdollar.desc: Regional banks have almost entirely domestic revenue with no overseas EPS translation drag. Higher US rates (which support the dollar via rate differential) expand net interest margins. Foreign capital flows into the US seeking higher yields directly increases bank deposits. Triple benefit.

strongdollar.r: ROIC 15.31%, GC:1 -- 90%+ domestic US revenue; strong dollar = zero EPS headwind + consumer flight to value
strongdollar.desc: Walmart derives ~90% of revenue from domestic US operations -- near-zero overseas translation drag from a rising dollar. Strong dollar often coincides with consumer price pressure globally, pushing domestic shoppers toward discount retailers. Grocery dominance = inelastic demand regardless.

strongdollar.r: ROIC 25.75%, Piotr:5 -- 27 countries seeking emergency dollar access (World Bank June 2026) = bond issuance surge
strongdollar.desc: Moody's benefits directly from Bretton Woods 2.0: as nations scramble for dollar access, they issue dollar-denominated sovereign bonds -- each requiring a Moody's rating. The 27 countries seeking emergency dollar access (World Bank June 2026) are all potential sovereign rating clients.

strongdollar.r: ROIC 44.25% -- global USD transaction volume; strong dollar = more USD cross-border fee value per transaction
strongdollar.desc: Counter-intuitive strong dollar play: Visa processes global transactions in USD. Strong dollar = each foreign-to-USD transaction conversion is worth more. Cross-border fees are a fixed % of transaction value in USD. Historically, strong DXY periods see Visa EPS beat as dollar-denominated fees amplify.

strongdollar.r: Nuclear power: 100% domestic USD revenue; AI data center contracts denominated in USD; wins in all scenarios
strongdollar.desc: Constellation Energy is scenario-agnostic because nuclear power is contracted in USD for US data centers. Strong dollar does not affect CEG as Microsoft and other hyperscaler contracts are denominated domestically. Nuclear is also an energy independence play -- reduces exposure to foreign oil.

strongdollar.r: Gulfstream + submarine yard — USD contracts, domestic industrial base
strongdollar.desc: General Dynamics is ships, combat vehicles, and Gulfstream. Almost all revenue is USD-denominated US government or domestic. Strong-dollar defense sleeve next to LMT/RTX/NOC.

strongdollar.r: C4ISR and munitions — US/NATO USD contracts, low overseas translation risk
strongdollar.desc: L3Harris sells sensors, radios, and munitions mostly to the US and NATO. Strong dollar and geopolitical spend both flow through USD contracts.

narrs.base: BASE CASE: Iran deal partially holds, oil settles $70-$80. Warsh stays hawkish through Q3, pivots Q4 as trimmed PCE data justifies cuts. Banks get SLR exemption in pipeline. Covert QE begins Q1 2027. Dollar weakens gradually. Markets chop sideways then rip higher late 2026.
narrs.bull: BULL — DEAL WORKS: Iran signed, Strait opens, oil crashes to $60s. Warsh's new real-time PCE shows 2.4% inflation. He cuts 75bps. Banks lever into treasuries via SLR deregulation. Dollar drops hard. Every Groman signal turns green simultaneously. S&P rips 20%+. Gold, BTC, Banks, Tech all win at once.
narrs.bear: BEAR — DEAL COLLAPSES: Israel escalates, Hormuz partially closes, oil spikes $100+. Warsh trapped — CPI re-accelerates to 6%+. Bond market revolts. 2Y hits 5.5%. S&P corrects 15-25% by Q4. Only energy tankers (FRO, STNG, DHT), gold miners, and commodities survive. New Fed chair -12% historical average in play.
narrs.qe: QE MACHINE FIRES: SLR deregulation passes. Banks buy $800B+ in US treasuries using leverage. Warsh points to new real-time AI data showing 2.1% inflation. Cuts 100bps. Balance sheet technically shrinks but covert QE surges. Dollar collapses. Bitcoin hits new ATH. Gold $5,000+. Stocks rip nominally while real purchasing power quietly erodes.
narrs.stag: STAGFLATION — 1970s REPLAY: Oil at $115, GDP stalls, CPI stuck at 6%+. Fed cannot cut (bond market revolt) or raise much further (debt load). Trapped. Real wages fall. This is the Volcker moment Warsh fears becoming. Only gold, energy, and consumer necessities provide real shelter. Bonds are the death trade.
narrs.strong: 💪 STRONG DOLLAR (Bretton Woods 2.0): Engineered global dollar shortage. DXY targeting 110. World chaos forces nations to spend on US goods and arms, requiring dollars. 27 countries sought emergency dollar access (World Bank June 2026). De-dollarization trade is DEAD. WINNERS: Defense (LMT +30%), Regional Banks (KRE +20%), Small Caps (IWM +12%), UUP ETF (+18%). AVOID: Gold (-15%), BTC (-30%), AAPL/KO/PG/MSFT (50-65% overseas revenue = EPS headwind).
narrs.carry: 🇯🇵 YEN CARRY TRADE UNWIND: BOJ shock-hikes to 1.75% while a weak US jobs print rattles confidence -- the exact combination that crashed USD/JPY from 161 to 141.70 in three weeks in August 2024 (Nikkei -12.4% in a single day, its worst since 1987). Leveraged funds that borrowed cheap yen to buy US tech, BTC, and EM assets face margin calls and forced liquidation. SAFE HAVENS: Yen itself (FXY +22%), long bonds (flight to quality +20%), gold miners (+18%). CARRY-FUNDED LOSERS: Leveraged AI/tech (NVDA -35%), Bitcoin (-35%), Emerging Markets (-22%), Regional Banks funding stress (-20%).
narrs.inflate: 💰🔥 INFLATE THE DEBT AWAY (Fiscal Dominance): The rollover wall forces the Fed's hand: ~$8T of debt reprices in 12 months and total debt (~$39.8T, ~122% of GDP) can't be serviced at 4-5% for long. The exit chosen every time debt gets this big — not default, not austerity, but financial repression: hold policy rates BELOW inflation, cap the long end with covert QE, and let a ~3% negative real rate quietly erode the debt's real value (the exact 1946-1951 + 1970s playbook that took debt/GDP from 120% to 30%). WINNERS: hard money — gold (GDX/NEM +30-40%), silver, BTC (+50%+), energy & real assets, TIPS. LOSERS: cash & long nominal bonds (TLT/ZROZ real value bleeds), savers & fixed salaries. Stocks rise nominally but ~flat in real terms (1970s). Not a forecast or advice — a mechanism model. See the Inflate-$ calculator below for the exact repression math.

angles.t: No Clear Driver — Quality Quietly Wins
angles.b: No single macro force is dominant. Size quality compounders (high ROIC, Piotroski 5+) and skip the narrative trades. Dump Top 20 here is almost pure business quality.

angles.t: Iran Deal + Oil Crash + Rate Cuts
angles.b: Oil to $58, Warsh pivots Q4, Groman signals green. S&P +16%, gold +20% (rebounds from pullbacks of the $5,500+ ATH), BTC +58% on dollar weakness. Buy the sequence: energy hedge OFF, gold ON, banks ON, tech ON.

angles.t: Deal Collapses -- DXY Spikes, Gold FALLS
angles.b: Oil $100+, Warsh hikes. DXY to 106 = dollar shortage intensifies. CRITICAL: gold falls in bear (DXY inverse confirmed). Only tankers, energy, and SHORT gold miners survive.

angles.t: Covert QE via SLR -- Dollar Collapses
angles.b: Banks buy bonds. Dollar collapses (DXY 90). ONLY scenario where gold/BTC win. BTC ATH. Gold $5000+. QE reverses the strong dollar thesis completely. Play hard assets hard.

Oil high, growth stalls, Fed trapped. DXY elevated (flight to safety) but real returns crushed. Bonds are the death trade. Only gold, energy, and necessities protect real wealth. Gold beats in stag even with strong dollar.

DXY targeting 110. World chaos forces spending on US goods/arms. Nations need dollars. 27 countries seeking emergency dollar access (World Bank June 2026). De-dollarization trade is DEAD. Buy domestic US revenue. Sell multinationals.

angles.t: Strong Dollar Winners vs Losers -- The Key Distinction
angles.b: Every 10% DXY rise shaves 2-4% off S&P EPS concentrated in multinationals. AVOID: AAPL (60% overseas), KO (65%), PG (55%), MSFT (50%). BUY: small caps, defense, regional banks, domestic staples. Rotate before the move.

angles.t: Yen Carry Trade Unwind -- The August 2024 Playbook Repeats
angles.b: BOJ hiked 25bp + weak US jobs data crashed USD/JPY from 161 to 141.70 in 3 weeks (Aug 2024), Nikkei -12.4% in a day. Fed-BOJ gap has narrowed from 525bp to ~263bp in 2026 -- less cushion, same trigger risk. Watch for BOJ surprise hikes paired with weak US data.

angles.t: Carry-Funded Assets Are the Hidden Risk in Every Portfolio
angles.b: Cheap yen leverage has quietly funded much of the 2024-2026 AI/tech rally and crypto positioning. When it unwinds, the assets that rallied hardest on liquidity (NVDA, BTC, high-beta growth) fall hardest. Bonds and yen itself are the natural hedge.

Policy rate pinned below CPI, QE caps the long end, dollar soft. Cash and nominal bonds bleed in real terms. Hard assets, gold, silver, and pricing-power staples defend purchasing power. This is the 1946-51 / 1970s mechanism, not a 12-month trade.
